subject: Pilot scope & hosted path: quickstart endpoints, rate envelope, and ops asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@parcelpilot.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope & hosted path: quickstart endpoints, rate envelope, and ops asks

Anna — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and recommended next steps so we can keep momentum on the pilot.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- ParcelPilot wants a fast hosted evaluation to validate extraction accuracy and routing latencies for the address-normalization flow.
- Expected peak: ~120 reqs/min with 1.5–2k token average per request for the next 2 weeks of pilot traffic.
- Primary blocking questions: rate ceilings for hosted trial, data residency (US-only), and whether dedicated capacity or VPC is required for PII-handling.

What we recommend for a first hosted pilot (low friction):
1) Hosted quickstart sandbox: we provision an isolated sandbox project with a dedicated API key, two endpoints (staging + canary), and a 14-day window. This gives realistic latency and token cost numbers without an infra commitment.
2) Rate envelope: we can start you at 150 reqs/min across the staging endpoint with a 500 concurrent token cap; can bump to 300 reqs/min for short bursts. If you need higher concurrency we can map to Dedicated.
3) Prefetch/prefix caching: enable prefix-KV caching for request types that share large prompts to cut per-token costs by ~30–40%. Karthik can propose caching config after we see a small sample of representative requests.
4) Data handling: hosted evaluation keeps transient request logs for up to 7 days by default; if ParcelPilot needs a longer retention or customer-managed KMS we should discuss Private/VPC.

Attachments: I attached a short matrix (quickstart-endpoint-matrix.csv) that maps endpoints, rate caps, and recommended token windows; and demo screens with the sample config we used.

Next steps / asks:
- Anna: confirm sandbox window (we propose start Mon 2028-09-25).
- ParcelPilot: share a sample traffic file (50–100 representative requests) so Karthik can propose caching + batch size.
- Redwood: we’ll provision sandbox + share staging API key and a short runbook with monitoring hooks.

If you already know you need an isolation guarantee (no transient logs retained >0 days, customer-managed keys), flag that now and we’ll route to Private/VPC early — otherwise hosted quickstart is the fastest path.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik on the caching config once we have the sample traffic.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Lopez <anna@parcelpilot.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Sep 2028 17:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & hosted path: quickstart endpoints, rate envelope, and ops asks

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Rate profile: 120 reqs/min steady state is correct for the first wave; we occasionally spike to ~260 reqs/min for 3–5 minute windows during batch processing jobs. Will your 300 reqs/min burst cover that?
2) Data residency: we need logs kept within US regions; 7 days is fine for the pilot, but for any production rollout we’ll need to discuss retention and KMS.
3) Isolation: ParcelPilot handles PII and our security team will likely push for either Dedicated or a Private VPC for production. For the pilot we are fine starting hosted as long as it’s an isolated sandbox with its own API key and clear retention limits.

Action from ParcelPilot: we’ll send a sample traffic file by EOD Monday (about 80 entries) and confirm the sandbox start date.

Also looping in ops@parcelpilot.com for scheduling — they’ll want the runbook and any test credentials.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Lopez
Product Manager, ParcelPilot
anna@parcelpilot.com | +1 617-555-4482

Subject: Re: Pilot scope & hosted path: quickstart endpoints, rate envelope, and ops asks

Anna / ops team — great, thanks for confirming. A couple follow-ups and concrete items from our ops side so we can provision: 

1) Burst handling: yes — we’ll set the sandbox staging endpoint to 300 reqs/min burst with a 20-second smoothing window. That should absorb the 3–5 minute spikes you mentioned. We’ll monitor and adjust if needed.
2) Staging endpoints: we will provide two endpoints —
   - staging.redwood.redwood-inference.com/v1/pp-staging (primary)
   - canary.redwood.redwood-inference.com/v1/pp-canary (for controlled rollouts)
3) Keys & runbook: expect a separate email early next week with the staging API key, a short ops runbook, and a monitoring snippet you can drop into your load tests.
4) Prefetch/caching: Karthik — when you get the sample file can you propose the prefix caching config and recommended batch sizes? If we can reduce average token consumption with caching the cost delta for a hosted pilot vs Dedicated will be clearer for ParcelPilot.
5) Security: for the pilot we’ll ensure US-region hosting and 7-day ephemeral log retention. If ParcelPilot security pushes for zero-retention or customer-managed KMS we’ll route to Private/VPC discussion with our security team and your secops.

Next steps (updated):
- ParcelPilot: sample traffic file by Mon 2028-09-25 (Anna).
- Redwood: provision sandbox, send staging API key + runbook, Karthik to send caching proposal after sample.
- Schedule: proposed pilot start Tue 2028-09-26 (can be shifted as needed).

I’ve attached the endpoint matrix again for easy reference. I’ll follow up with the provisioning email earliest Monday morning.

—
Marissa Cole
